EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: The order-book-imbalance Sharpe results appear to describe the same achievement under different entries and dates.
items.because: Northpeak and Kaggle report overlapping gains and 18-month out-of-sample periods.

items.says: The most recent bakery role draws attention away from the quantitative research direction.
items.because: Its position can attract attention before the more relevant quantitative work.

items.says: The labour-budget result has no figure showing how much or how consistently costs were controlled.
The unsold-bread reduction is buried after the methods instead of leading the line.
The 35% improvement does not identify its comparison.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether it is relative to the unsmoothed signal, another benchmark, or a different period.

items.says: The validation description gives no result or decision it supported.
items.because: A reader can see how the signal was tested but cannot tell what the validation showed.

items.says: The closing explanation repeats the safeguards already named.
items.because: It restates what the safeguards are intended to ensure and pushes the missing result further back.

items.says: The feature-store reuse result is delayed in a relative clause.
The live allocation’s scale is unclear.
The approval is buried in a trailing clause.
The best backtested Sharpe from 400 configurations is not a valid estimate of expected live Sharpe as written.
items.because: Selecting the top result creates selection bias, and the line describes no correction or separate validation.

items.says: The selected Sharpe has no stated value or comparison.
The indirect ending makes the result difficult to scan.
The Sharpe improvement is buried after several signal and evaluation details.
items.because: Readers encounter the central outcome only after the instrument, signal, horizon, and testing qualifiers.

items.says: Using the same random seed on every worker can produce duplicate or overlapping random-number sequences.
items.because: Identically initialized workers may not produce independent Monte Carlo replicates.

items.says: “Running the runs” is repetitive.
“My proof” uses a first-person possessive.
“My proof” redundantly restates the derivation.
The bound-tightening result does not open the bullet.
The past-tense “Beat” conflicts with the present-tense framing of an ongoing study.
The crisis-period significance claim is not supported by the stated Holm correction across the 30 index tests.
items.because: Significance within crisis subperiods requires period-specific tests and a correction covering those tests; the wording also does not clarify whether each period was tested separately.

items.says: The main significance result follows the methods and correction.
items.because: Readers reach the key outcome only after those details, making it easier to miss.

items.says: The past-tense “Tested” conflicts with the present-tense framing of an ongoing study.
The past-tense “Wrote” conflicts with the present-tense framing of an ongoing study.
“Which was presented” uses passive voice without naming the presenter.
The competition modeling work has no stated result.
items.because: Without an outcome, the contribution is difficult to evaluate.

items.says: The 0.02 gap does not identify the score metric.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the number measures.

items.says: The line does not say whether 0.02 is the gap before or after the change.
items.because: Without before-and-after context, a reader cannot tell how much closer the scores became.

items.says: The result follows the method and a relative clause instead of leading the line.
items.because: Leading with it would make the result quicker to scan.

items.says: The 0.4 Sharpe increase does not name its comparison.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether it is relative to the book without the signal or another benchmark.

items.says: The method precedes the result.
items.because: The signal and testing details make the result slower to find.

items.says: “Econometircs” is misspelled.
items.because: The spelling error is visible in a skills heading and can distract from the technical content.
